guard: a legacy manager report stops update before the extension mutation pass or a replay subprocess
why: The old packaged-manager fixture proves a real published manager without the custody seam receives the report and is left alive. This focused kernel cell proves the updater's decision boundary: a legacy report returns before the global seed store is rewritten, before the extension mutation lock, and before any extension replay subprocess.

The mutation removes only the legacy stop so a none verdict still continues. Since #1620 the observation precedes the seed reconcile, so the earliest red that observes fallthrough is the seed-store assertion rather than the mutation-pass one.

mutations.name: M1 ignore the legacy verdict and continue the update replay
mutations.expectRed: a legacy custody verdict refuses BEFORE the seed store is rewritten
mutations.cell: a running legacy manager is reported, then blocks an update before replay
mutations.note: The result remains type-correct. A none verdict still continues. A legacy verdict falls through to the seed reconcile and then to claimUpdatePass. The named cell's first forbidden assertion is the observation; since #1620 moved the reconcile after the report, that is the seed-store assertion.
